mechanism_narrative: TGFBR2 (Ser/Thr kinase) and TNFRSF1A (death receptor, no kinase) are forced into proximity by a flexible GS4 linker (~20 A). TGFBR2's constitutive kinase transphosphorylates TNFRSF1A's intracellular domain at atypical Ser/Thr sites, creating hybrid docking surfaces. The biased output retains SMAD2/3-SMAD4 transcriptional signaling (via TGFBR2->SMAD2/3) and NF-kB survival signaling (via TNFRSF1A->TRADD->TRAF2->RIPK1->IKK), but sterically excludes the proapoptotic FADD/CASP8 DISC complex (requires precise death-domain geometry disrupted by co-clustering) and GRB2/SHC1/PLCG1 adaptors (require tyrosine-phosphorylated motifs absent from both receptors). This yields a TGF-beta/TNF hybrid signal biased toward matrix remodeling and survival over apoptosis and inflammation.
